posts.title: Record a browser task, then replay it
posts.promise: Capture a repeat task once and replay or export its steps.
posts.whatItIs: Waystone is a browser action recorder. Its README says a person can record a task and get numbered instructions, screenshots, workflow data, and browser commands. The commands can replay the task or be exported as Playwright or Puppeteer scripts. A beginner could make a small version for one stable public form or listing.
posts.whoPays: Hypothesis: small teams that repeat browser tasks might pay for a tailored tool; the source does not establish customers or demand.
loop: A person records one browser task.
Save the steps, element selectors, and screenshots.
Replay the steps in a browser or export a script.
Capture results and flag steps that fail.
A person checks results and updates the recording when the site changes.
posts.evidence: The project README describes recording, replay, screenshots, JSON workflow output, and script export. It lists scraping, data collection, and repetitive office tasks as possible uses; these are project documentation, not verified customer outcomes.
posts.uncertainty: The README does not establish paid use or reliable operation across changing sites. A student version should use a low-risk site and avoid credentials or consequential actions. Humans select the task, handle access controls and errors, and verify results.
first24Hours: Install a browser automation library and open a local demo page.
Record and replay one harmless form interaction.
Save a screenshot and note which page changes break replay.

ease.reason: README lists browser recording and script export; a small single-site prototype is approachable.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: small teams may pay to repeat browser tasks; demand is unproved.

feasibility.reason: A two-week prototype can record and replay one stable form, with site changes as a limit.

autonomy.reason: Recorded replay automates repeated clicks; humans choose tasks and handle login, errors, and site changes.

evidence.reason: README details outputs and use cases; real customer use is not established.

posts.title: Make a repeatable diagram with an AI skill
posts.promise: Turn a plain request into one editable HTML and SVG diagram.
posts.whatItIs: Diagram Design is an agent skill for making diagrams as a self-contained HTML and SVG file. Its README lists 44 diagram types and examples such as architecture and sequence diagrams. The skill can also use a site palette and fonts for styling. A beginner could build a smaller skill with a few templates and a simple export page.
posts.whoPays: Hypothesis: product teams that make diagrams often may pay for a consistent workflow; the source does not show who pays or whether demand exists.
loop: A user describes the information and diagram type.
The agent selects a matching template.
It writes an HTML file with SVG shapes and labels.
The user opens the file and checks labels and relationships.
The user corrects errors and exports or shares the diagram.
posts.evidence: The README provides installation instructions, sample prompts, supported coding agents, and the claimed single-file HTML/SVG output. These establish documented product behavior, not sales or measured customer use.
posts.uncertainty: The source does not establish demand or the accuracy of generated diagrams. The small version can automate drafting and formatting, while a person must verify that every connection and label is correct and that the styling fits the brand.
first24Hours: Install an agent skill host and create one basic flowchart template.
Generate a diagram from a short sample request.
Open the HTML file and check labels, arrows, and readability.

ease.reason: README shows installation and example requests; a small template set is accessible.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: teams may pay for faster branded diagrams; demand is unproved.

feasibility.reason: Two weeks can produce a few HTML/SVG diagram templates; brand onboarding remains manual.

autonomy.reason: Agent drafts diagrams from requests; a person must check correctness and visual quality.

evidence.reason: README documents workflow and output format; it does not establish customer use.

steps.message: Reviewed eight enriched product leads against the prior-post index. Picked Waystone for a bounded browser replay loop and Diagram Design for a clear, beginner-testable file-generation workflow; demand remains hypothetical.
